name: Clay
summary: Waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows for go-to-market teams. It enriches rather than sends, so you still need a separate email tool.
best_for: modern GTM and ops teams who want best-in-class waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows — and have someone to own it
skip_if: you want to sign up and prospect on day one, or you can't dedicate time to learn it — the curve and credit spend frustrate casual users
honest_knock: Two honest catches: a steep learning curve (expect 2–4 weeks, many teams need a dedicated Clay expert), and credits that are hard to forecast at scale. It's an enrichment engine, not a sender — you still need Instantly, Lemlist or Outreach to actually email.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-14 on their own pricing page; both billing terms read from the page markup, and no figure has moved since our August reading) Clay meters two things separately — actions and data credits — and each paid plan is an expandable volume rather than a fixed tier, which is the part most write-ups still get wrong, ours included until the August 2026 update. The free plan is real: 6,000 actions and 1,200 data credits a year, unlimited seats and tables, multi-provider waterfalls and Claygent, capped at 200 rows per table and with no phone enrichment. Launch is advertised at $167/mo but starts at $54/mo on annual billing or $60 monthly, and Growth at $446/mo but starts at $185/mo annually or $205 monthly — the headline is a configured volume, not the floor, so read the ladder rather than the card. Billed monthly the Launch action ladder runs $60, $150, $200, $290 and $540 for 15K, 40K, 60K, 100K and 200K actions a month; billed annually it runs $54, $135, $180, $261 and $486 a month for 180K, 480K, 720K, 1.2M and 2.4M actions a year. Growth starts one rung higher: $205, $290, $450 and $850 a month for 40K to 200K monthly actions, or $185 to $765 a month on the annual ladder. Data credits are a separate meter again — monthly from $125 for 2,500 credits up to $2,125 for 50,000, or annually from $113/mo for 30,000 a year up to $1,913/mo for 600,000. Annual billing saves 10%. Waterfall enrichment spends credits per lookup, so the credit meter rather than the plan is what decides the bill. One discrepancy is worth carrying to checkout, and it survived this reading: the plan FAQ at the bottom of the page describes Launch as “starting at $185/mo”, which is not the Launch floor of $54 but the Growth one. Enterprise is quote-only.
